'''Arron Agustin Afflalo''' (born October 15, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. As a junior, he was named a consensus [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|player of the year]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. After forgoing his senior year in college, Afflalo was selected in the first round of the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 27th overall pick.

==Early life==
Afflalo was born at the [[UCLA Medical Center]] in [[Los Angeles, California]], only a few minutes' walk from [[Pauley Pavilion]], where the UCLA Bruins play their home games. His parents are Benjamin Afflalo and Gwendolyn Washington. He also has a younger sister named Paris.<ref>[http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=208184926 #4 Arron Afflalo]</ref> Afflalo has grandparents from Jamaica and is also of Portuguese and Moroccan descent.<ref name=norwood /> He is named after the Biblical figure [[Aaron]], but his mother changed the spelling to make it unique.<ref name=norwood />

Afflalo's parents did not marry and separated when he was three.<ref name=norwood>{{cite web |last1=Norwood |first1=Robyn |title=They're well-connected |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2007-feb-01-sp-afflalo1-story.html |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=October 7, 2023 |date=February 1, 2007}}</ref> He lived with his mother until the age of 13 and then moved into his father's house in [[Compton, California]].<ref name=norwood /> Afflalo grew up as a fan of the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], and his favourite player was [[Byron Scott]]; Afflalo wore a #4 jersey in honor of Scott, who used the same number.<ref name=norwood />

As a senior in the 2003–04 season, Afflalo helped lead [[Centennial High School (Compton, California)|Centennial High School]] to a California Division III title.

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Afflalo was listed as the No. 6 shooting guard and the No. 26 player in the nation in 2004.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Arron-Afflalo-16932 Arron Afflalo – Yahoo! Sports]</ref>

==College career==
As a collegiate player for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], Afflalo's defensive dominance throughout the [[2006–07 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2006–07 season]] (one example being holding Cal's [[Ayinde Ubaka]] to zero points in one of the two teams' matchups), and his 17.4 points per game, led to him being voted the [[Pac-10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-10 Player of the Year]] by the other coaches in the conference.<ref name=poy/> He also set the then-school record for most [[three-point field goal]]s made (87) in a season.{{#tag:ref|The record stood for eight years until [[Bryce Alford]] broke it in [[2014–15 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2015]].<ref name=wang_03192015>{{cite news|last=Wang |first=Jack |title=NCAA Tournament: Bryce Alford gets hot and fortunate as UCLA stuns SMU |date=March 19, 2015 |newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News |url=http://www.dailynews.com/events/20150319/ncaa-tournament-bryce-alford-gets-hot-and-fortunate-as-ucla-stuns-smu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150322133534/http://www.dailynews.com/events/20150319/ncaa-tournament-bryce-alford-gets-hot-and-fortunate-as-ucla-stuns-smu |archive-date=March 22, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} Commenting on the award, Afflalo said, "It is good that contributions on both ends of the floor are recognized ... If you truly have a love and passion for the game, then you should work at every aspect of it, not just the part that gives you [attention], that being scoring."<ref name="poy">{{Cite web |last=Pucin |first=Diane |date=2007-03-06 |title=Afflalo is player of year |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2007-mar-06-sp-awards6-story.html |access-date=2025-05-03 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref>

===NCAA tournament===
In a 2006 NCAA tournament game against [[University of Alabama|Alabama]], Afflalo hit the game-winning three-point shot<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121025180824/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000013 Farmar's five 3s have UCLA heading to Oakland] "Afflalo got loose and launched a 3-pointer, keeping UCLA ahead 60–56 with 34 seconds left."</ref> and also defended Alabama point guard [[Ronald Steele]] on his errant three-point attempt, which would have given Alabama the lead.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/101764224/fort-worth-star-telegram/ |title=UCLA holds on when Alabama misfires at end |page=3CC |first=Beth |last=Harris |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 19, 2006 |accessdate=May 13, 2022 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

In the Bruins' 2006 Sweet Sixteen comeback victory over [[Gonzaga University|Gonzaga]], Afflalo and teammate [[Ryan Hollins]], in what was later widely hailed as a classy move, helped the distraught Gonzaga star [[Adam Morrison]] off the court after the final buzzer sounded.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120714123505/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000014|title=UCLA scores final 11 points in stunning comeback over Gonzaga}} "Hollins and Afflalo went to help up Morrison, who was spread on the floor at midcourt."</ref><ref>[http://www.beloblog.com/ProJo_Blogs/hoops/archives/2006/03 Who was George Mason?] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060709085821/http://www.beloblog.com/ProJo_Blogs/hoops/archives/2006/03 |date=July 9, 2006 }}</ref> Against [[University of Memphis|Memphis]] in the [[Elite Eight]], Afflalo was noted by many to be largely responsible for stopping [[Rodney Carney]] and helping UCLA advance to the [[Final Four]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120713220213/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=264000015|title=Afflalo, UCLA clamp down on Memphis, stamp Final Four ticket}} "Afflalo scored 15 points and shut down Memphis leading scorer Rodney Carney, helping No. 2 seed UCLA defeat the top-seeded Tigers"</ref>

In the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007 NCAA Tournament]], he was named the West Regional's Most Outstanding Player after scoring 24 points and making several big plays in a 68–55 victory over the [[Kansas Jayhawks]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120717203100/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000015|title=Afflalo plays big, takes UCLA to NCAA-record 17th Final Four}}</ref> However, his quick foul trouble against the Florida Gators cost his team the ability to successfully compete, and the Bruins ended up bowing out of the tournament.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121025180849/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000031 Florida runs over UCLA, sets up another battle with Ohio St.] "Bruins guard Arron Afflalo sat on the bench for almost the entire first half with foul trouble"</ref>

==Professional career==

===Detroit Pistons (2007–2009)===
On June 28, 2007, Afflalo was drafted with the 27th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the Detroit Pistons and later signed July 6.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2007_08/ NBA Transactions: 2007–08]</ref> In a surprising turn of events, Afflalo made his first career NBA start on November 1, 2007, the opening night of his rookie season, when [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]] missed the first two games to attend the birth of his son. Afflalo started the team's first and second games during his rookie campaign<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/afflalo_080711.html?DB_OEM_ID=30500 Arron's Evolution: In second season, Afflalo expects to flash more offense]</ref> that culminated with a loss to the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] Finals of the [[2008 NBA Playoffs]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs2008/series?series=detbos ESPN: 2008 ECF]</ref>

On February 14, 2009, Afflalo helped Team Detroit to its second victory in three years at the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Shooting Stars Competition|Shooting Stars Competition]] during the [[2009 NBA All-Star Game|2009 NBA All-Star Weekend]] in Phoenix, Arizona. Afflalo teamed with [[Detroit Shock]] head coach and former NBA legend [[Bill Laimbeer]], and Shock guard [[Katie Smith]] to get the win against Team Phoenix in the final.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2009/allstar2009/01/16/haier.shooting.stars/index.html |title=Phoenix team falters from downtown, Detroit takes title |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-06-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120211080301/http://www.nba.com/2009/allstar2009/01/16/haier.shooting.stars/index.html |archive-date=2012-02-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref>[[File:Arron Afflalo Nuggets.jpg|thumb|right|Afflalo with the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2011|267x267px]]
===Denver Nuggets (2009–2012)===
On July 13, 2009, he was traded along with [[Walter Sharpe]] to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for a second-round pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] and cash.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/afflalo_sharpe_trade_071309.html |title=Nuggets Acquire Afflalo, Sharpe from Detroit |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 13, 2009 |access-date=July 14, 2009}}</ref> The draft pick became the 52nd overall pick and was used by the Pistons to draft [[Vernon Macklin]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/afflaar01.html Arron Afflalo NBA & ABA Stats]</ref>

On February 10, 2011, Afflalo made a 20-foot jump shot at the buzzer over [[Shawn Marion]] as the Nuggets defeated the [[2011 NBA Finals|eventual NBA champion]] [[Dallas Mavericks]] 121–120, in a game that would be [[Carmelo Anthony]]’s final Denver home game. The Nuggets trailed by as many as 13 in the 4th quarter and were down 119–110 with under 2 minutes to play before pulling off a miraculous upset victory. Afflalo had 19 points in the fourth quarter alone to almost single-handedly power Denver to the win, ending Dallas’ ten game win streak.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110213061154/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310210007 Arron Afflalo's buzzer-beater helps Nuggets bury Mavs]</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2012–2014)===
On August 10, 2012, he was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] in a four-team deal which sent [[Dwight Howard]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Andrew Bynum]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and [[Andre Iguodala]] to the Nuggets.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-six-players-five-draft-picks-howard-trade Magic Acquire Six Players, Five Draft Picks in Howard Trade]</ref>
[[File:Arron Afflalo Washington at Orlando 029.jpg|thumb|270x270px|Afflalo with the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2012]]
On December 3, 2013, he recorded a career-high 43 points and minutes with 52, in a double-overtime loss to the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131203/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Sixers 126, Magic 125 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2013-12-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131207092224/http://www.nba.com/games/20131203/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2013-12-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His previous career-high in points came just less than a month earlier with 36 points against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on November 13,<ref>[https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2013/12/04/arron-afflalo-career-high-video-magic-sixers Magic's Arron Afflalo scores a career-high 43 points in loss to Sixers]</ref> where he also made a career-high 8 three-point shots.<ref>[http://www.magicbasketballonline.com/2013/11/13/arron-afflalos-courageous-effort-propels-magic-past-bucks/ Arron Afflalo's "Courageous Effort" Propels Magic Past Bucks]</ref>

===Return to the Nuggets (2014–2015)===
On June 26, 2014, Afflalo was traded back to the Denver Nuggets in exchange for [[Evan Fournier]] and the draft rights to [[Devyn Marble]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-arron-afflalo-trade-orlando Nuggets Acquire Arron Afflalo in Trade with Orlando]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16082 |title=Magic trade Arron Afflalo to Nuggets |access-date=2014-06-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304061048/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16082 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Afflalo, arguably Orlando's best player in 2013–14, was dealt to avoid concerns that he would opt out of his contract following the 2014–15 season and assured the Magic value in return. The transaction also cleared $6 million in cap space for the team.<ref>[http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/blogs/magic-basketblog/os-mbb-magic-trade-arron-afflalo-20140626,0,3989296.post Magic trade Arron Afflalo to Nuggets for Evan Fournier and the draft's 56th pick]</ref>

On October 29, 2014, Afflalo made his return for the Nuggets, recording 15 points and four rebounds in the season opening 89–79 win over the Detroit Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/DETDEN/gameinfo.html |title=Nuggets open with 89–79 win over Pistons |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150125170633/http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/DETDEN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-01-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2015)===
On February 19, 2015, Afflalo was traded, along with [[Alonzo Gee]], to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Will Barton]], [[Víctor Claver]], [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]], and a lottery-protected 2016 first-round pick.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-arron-afflalo-and-alonzo-gee-denver Trail Blazers Acquire Arron Afflalo And Alonzo Gee From Denver]</ref>

===New York Knicks (2015–2016)===
On July 9, 2015, Afflalo signed with the [[New York Knicks]]. The move reunited him with his former [[Denver Nuggets]] teammate [[Carmelo Anthony]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-acquire-four-free-agents-afflalo-r.-lopez-williams-oquinn|title=Knicks Acquire Four Free Agents: Afflalo, R. Lopez, Williams, O'Quinn|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 10, 2015}}</ref> Afflalo missed the first eight games of the regular season with hamstring issues, making his debut for the Knicks on November 11 against the Charlotte Hornets. In 28 minutes as a starter, he recorded 12 points and 6 rebounds in a 95–93 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151111/NYKCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Hornets' Zeller hits layup with 0.6 left to top Knicks 95–93|work=NBA.com|date=November 11, 2015|access-date=November 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151112050247/http://www.nba.com/games/20151111/NYKCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 12, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Over his first nine games for the Knicks, Afflalo averaged just 11.2 points per game. He went on to score a season-high 31 points in an overtime loss to the Houston Rockets on November 29.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151129/HOUNYK/gameinfo.html|title=Rockets rally in fourth, beat Knicks 116–111 in overtime|work=NBA.com|date=November 29, 2015|access-date=November 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151127050342/http://www.nba.com/games/20151129/HOUNYK/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 27, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He topped that mark with 38 points against the Atlanta Hawks on January 3, hitting 14-of-17 from the field and 7-of-8 from three-point range.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160103/ATLNYK/gameinfo.html|title=Afflalo scores 38, Knicks beat Hawks 111–97|work=NBA.com|date=January 3, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2016}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2016–2017)===
On July 9, 2016, Afflalo signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-four-free-agents|title=Kings Sign Four Free Agents|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2016|access-date=July 9, 2016}}</ref> On June 23, 2017, he was waived by the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-arron-afflalo|title=Kings Waive Arron Afflalo|work=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2017|access-date=June 23, 2017}}</ref>

===Return to Orlando (2017–2018)===
On July 27, 2017, Afflalo signed with the [[Orlando Magic]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-arron-afflalo|title=Magic Sign Arron Afflalo|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2017|access-date=July 27, 2017}}</ref> On January 16, 2018, Afflalo was involved in an on-court fight with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]' [[Nemanja Bjelica]]; he took a [[Swing (boxing)|swing]] on Bjelica but Bjelica evaded it and put Afflalo in a headlock to calm him down.<ref name="january2018fine">{{cite news |last1=Wells |first1=Adam |title=Arron Afflalo Suspended 2 Games for Fight with Nemanja Bjelica |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2754851-arron-afflalo-suspended-2-games-for-fight-with-nemanja-bjelica |access-date=17 September 2019 |work=bleacherreport.com |date=18 January 2018}}</ref> Afflalo later received a two-game suspension for his actions.<ref name="january2018fine" /> Afflalo finished the season with career-lows of 3.4 points, 1.2 rebounds and 0.6 assists over 53 games.

==Personal life==
Afflalo attended [[Centennial High School (Compton, California)|Centennial High School]] two years ahead of rapper [[Kendrick Lamar]], who credited Afflalo's academic and athletic achievements in the first verse of the song "Black Boy Fly", a bonus track from his album ''[[Good Kid, M.A.A.D City]]''. In the song, Lamar described Afflalo as an example of someone who had the "determination, ambition plus dedication and wisdom" to get out of Compton.

Afflalo nodded towards Lamar's drive in an interview with [[XXL (magazine)|XXL]], saying "I was almost like the golden child in the city of Compton, or at least at Centennial at that time, considering where I was as a basketball player, and all the positivity I had around me, in terms of school and people appreciating me and showing me love for what I did on the court and in the community at that time in my life. So for him to kind of be in the background and who he is today, it showed you the perseverance that he had for so many years."<ref>{{cite web|last1=XXL Staff|title=NBA Star Arron Afflalo Responds to Kendrick Lamar's "Black Boy Fly" Shout-Out |url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2012/11/arron-afflalo-kendrick-lamar-black-boy-fly/|website=XXL Magazine|date=5 November 2012 |access-date=5 August 2016}}</ref>
